name: Add Multiple Rows
description: Add multiple rows of data to a Google Sheet. [See the documentation](https://developers.google.com/sheets/api/reference/rest/v4/spreadsheets.values/append)

configurable_props.name: drive
configurable_props.label: Drive
configurable_props.description: Defaults to `My Drive`. To select a [Shared Drive](https://support.google.com/a/users/answer/9310351) instead, select it from this list.

configurable_props.name: sheetId
configurable_props.label: Spreadsheet ID
configurable_props.description: Select a spreadsheet or provide a spreadsheet ID

configurable_props.name: worksheetId
configurable_props.label: Worksheet ID
configurable_props.description: Select a worksheet or provide a worksheet ID

configurable_props.name: rowsDescription
configurable_props.content: Each nested array should represent a row, with each element of the nested array representing a cell/column value (e.g., passing `[["Foo",1,2],["Bar",3,4]]` will insert two rows of data with three columns each). The most common pattern is to reference an array of arrays exported by a previous step (e.g., `{{steps.foo.$return_value}}`). You may also enter or construct a string that will `JSON.parse()` to an array of arrays.

configurable_props.name: resetRowFormat
configurable_props.label: Reset Row Format
configurable_props.description: Reset the formatting of the rows that were added (line style to none, background to white, foreground color to black, font size to 10, no bold, no italic, no strikethrough, horizontalAlignment to left). This is useful if you want to add rows to a formatted table in Google Sheets.
